questions.q_en: Shivaji reduced the powers of the existing deshmuks and kulkarnis. He appointed his own revenue officials called _______
questions.solution_en:
• The revenue system of Shivaji was based on that of Malik Amber of Ahmadnagar.

• Lands were measured by using the measuring rod called kathi.

• Lands were also classified into three categories - paddy fields, garden lands and hilly tracks.

• He reduced the powers of the existing deshmuks and kulkarnis. He appointed his own revenue officials called karkuns.

• Chauth and sardeshmukhi were the taxes collected not in the Maratha kingdom but in the neighbouring territories of the Mughal empire or Deccan sultanates.

• Chauth was one fourth of the land revenue paid to the Marathas in order to avoid the Maratha raids. Sardeshmukhi was an additional levy of ten percent on those lands which the Marathas claimed hereditary rights.

questions.q_en: Which of the following Maratha families is mentioned as influential before the rise of Shivaji?
questions.solution_en:
Before the rise of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the Mores of Javali and the Nimbalkars of Phaltan were prominent Maratha families with significant local power in the Western Ghats region.

• The Mores controlled the Javali valley, a strategic area later captured by Shivaji in 1656, which helped him expand his foothold in the Konkan.

• The Nimbalkars were influential in Phaltan (southern Maharashtra) and often allied with the Adil Shahis of Bijapur before aligning with the Marathas.

questions.q_en: Which Peshwa established the system of confederacy among the Maratha chiefs?
options_en: Shahji Bhonsle and his son Shivaji
questions.solution_en:
• After the death of Chhatrapati Shahu (1749), the Peshwa became the de facto ruler, and regional Maratha chiefs (like Holkars, Shindes, Bhonsles, and Gaekwads) gained semi-autonomous power.

• Balaji Baji Rao formalized this decentralized system, allowing chiefs to govern their territories while coordinating under Peshwa's leadership for military and political goals.

Further insights:

• Baji Rao was the eldest son of Balaji Viswanath. He succeeded his father as Peshwa at the age young age of twenty. The Maratha power reached its zenith under him.

• He initiated the system of confederacy among the Maratha chiefs.

• Under this system, each Maratha chief was assigned a territory which could be administered autonomously.

• As a result, many Maratha families became prominent and established their authority in different parts of India. They were the Gaekwad at Baroda, the Bhonsle at Nagpur, the Holkars at Indore, the Scindias at Gwalior, and the Peshwas at Poona.

questions.q_en: According to the Treaty of Purandar, how many forts did Shivaji have to surrender to the Mughals out of the 35 he held?
questions.solution_en:
According to the Treaty of Purandar (1665), signed between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Mughal general Jai Singh I, Shivaji had to surrender 23 out of the 35 forts he controlled at the time.

The remaining 12 forts were to be left to Shivaji on condition of service and loyalty to the Mughal empire.

• In the infantry, the Mavli foot soldiers played an important role. Shivaji also maintained a navy.

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding Shivaji's administration.

a. Shivaji was the central figure in the government and was assisted by a council of eight ministers called Ashtapradhan.

b. Each minister in the Ashtapradhan was solely responsible to the council as a whole.

c. Shivaji's revenue system was based on that of Malik Amber of Ahmadnagar.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_en:
The Ashtapradhan (Council of Eight Ministers) advised Shivaji on governance, military, finance, and justice. Key ministers included:

• Peshwa (Prime Minister)

• Amatya (Finance Minister)

• Senapati (Commander-in-Chief)

• Mantri (Chronicler/Diplomat)

The ministers were directly accountable to Shivaji, not the council. The Ashtapradhan was an advisory body, but ultimate authority rested with the king.

The revenue system of Shivaji was based on that of Malik Amber of Ahmadnagar.

questions.q_en: Shivaji faced defeat and lost Poona under which Mughal governor of the Deccan sent by Aurangazeb?
questions.solution_en:
• Shaista Khan (Aurangzeb's maternal uncle) was appointed as the Mughal governor of the Deccan in 1660 to crush Shivaji's rebellion.

• In 1663, Shivaji lost Poona (Pune) to Shaista Khan, who occupied Shivaji's ancestral Lal Mahal palace.

• However, in a daring night raid (April 1663), Shivaji attacked Shaista Khan in Pune, cutting his fingers and killing his son. This forced Shaista Khan to retreat.

• Raja Jai Singh defeated Shivaji later (1665) at Purandar, but Shaista Khan was the first Mughal governor to temporarily seize Poona.

questions.q_en: For the second time, Surat was plundered by Shivaji in which year?
questions.solution_en:
Shivaji plundered Surat for the second time in 1670 (specifically October 1670).

First Sack of Surat (1664):

• Shivaji's first attack on Surat (Mughal Empire's richest port) shocked the Mughals and boosted Maratha resources.

Second Sack of Surat (1670):

• After escaping Mughal captivity (1666) and rebuilding his power, Shivaji re-attacked Surat in 1670 to weaken Aurangzeb's finances.

• The Mughal governor, Inayat Khan, fled again, and the Marathas looted the city unopposed.

Significance:

• The 1670 plunder reaffirmed Maratha dominance and funded Shivaji's campaigns to recapture lost forts (like Sinhagad, Purandar).

questions.q_en: Under whose reign the Peshwas rose to power?
questions.solution_en:
• There ensued a war of succession after the death of Shivaji between his sons, Shambaji and Rajaram.

• Shambaji emerged victorious but later he was captured and executed by the Mughals.

• Rajaram succeeded the throne but the Mughals made him to flee to the Ginjee fort. He died at Satara. He was succeeded by his minor son Shivaji II with his mother Tara Bai as regent.

• The next ruler was Shahu in whose reign the Peshwas rose to power.

questions.q_en: Which Maratha queen led resistance against the Mughals after her husband's (Rajaram) death?
questions.solution_en:
:

• Tarabai, widow of Rajaram, fiercely defended the Maratha Empire against Aurangzeb during the War of 27 Years (1682 - 1707)

• After Rajaram died in 1700, Tarabai took command of the Maratha forces and continued the resistance against the Mughal Empire during a critical period.

• She declared her young son Shivaji II as the successor and skillfully managed both military operations and administrative affairs.

• Under her leadership, the Marathas effectively employed guerrilla tactics against Aurangzeb's forces, preventing the Mughals from completely conquering Maratha territories despite their numerical superiority.

• Her leadership lasted until 1707 and was crucial in preserving Maratha independence during a very challenging time.

questions.q_en: Shivaji was born at Shivaner in which year?
questions.solution_en:

• He inherited the jagir of Poona from his father in 1637.

questions.q_en: At what age did Balaji Baji Rao become Peshwa?
questions.solution_en:
• Balaji Baji Rao succeeded his father as Peshwa at the young age of nineteen. The Maratha king Shahu died in 1749 without issue. His nominated successor Ramraja was imprisoned by the Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao at Satara.

• The full control of the Maratha kingdom came under the Peshwa.

• Peshwa entered into an agreement with the Mughal Emperor in 1752.

• According to it the Peshwa gave assurance to the Mughal Emperor that he would protect the Mughal Empire from internal and external enemies for which the Chauth of the northwest provinces and the total revenue of the Agra and Ajmer provinces would be collected by the Marathas.

• Thus when Ahmad Shah Abdali invaded India, it became the responsibility of the Marathas to protect India.
